data.purpose: Every number, price, percentage, and quoted citation — the 'this is verifiable' register.

shadows.name: hero-lift
shadows.purpose: The comparison chart card only — the page's single most important proof element.

motion.name: chart-fill
motion.purpose: One-time bar-fill reveal on scroll-into-view via transform:scaleX(), never width. Respects prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Solid engineered-blue pill, used for Register/primary actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; text-decoration: none; font-family: Manrope, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 16px; border-radius: 999px; padding: 14px 30px; background: #1345C0; color: #fff; border: 1.5px solid transparent; transition: background .15s, transform .1s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #0D3391; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(.98); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2.5px solid #1345C0; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Outline pill, used for Log in / secondary actions.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 8px; text-decoration: none; font-family: Manrope, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 16px; border-radius: 999px; padding: 14px 30px; background: transparent; color: #0B1220; border: 1.5px solid #C7D2E0; transition: border-color .15s, color .15s, transform .1s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: #1345C0; color: #1345C0; } .ds-btn-ghost:active { transform: scale(.98); }

components.name: Comparison Chart Row
components.description: Signature component: one row of the hero comparison chart (label, animated fill track, mono percentage).
components.css: .ds-chart-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 16px; margin-bottom: 16px; font-family: Manrope, sans-serif; } .ds-chart-label { width: 132px; flex-shrink: 0; font-weight: 700; font-size: 14.5px; color: #0B1220; } .ds-chart-track { flex: 1; height: 30px; background: #F5F8FC; border-radius: 6px; overflow: hidden; position: relative; } .ds-chart-fill { position: absolute; inset: 0 auto 0 0; width: var(--w); border-radius: 6px; background: #1345C0; transform: scaleX(1); transform-origin: left center; } .ds-chart-pct { width: 56px; flex-shrink: 0; text-align: right; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-weight: 700; font-size: 17px; color: #0B1220; }

components.name: Citation Block
components.description: Verified-tint quote block replacing a colored border-left accent; used wherever the product shows a source citation.
components.html: "Revenue was 500,000 euros in 2025." — quoted verbatim from the uploaded document
components.css: .ds-cite { padding: 14px 16px; border-radius: 8px; background: #E9F7EE; color: #166534; font-size: 13.5px; font-style: italic; line-height: 1.5; }

narrative.overview:
vanKonijnenburg reads financial documents and answers questions about them, backing every claim with an exact citation from the source — the product's entire pitch is that you verify it yourself instead of trusting a black box. The visual system takes that literally: it borrows the grammar of an audit workpaper — precise rows, tabular numerals, a single functional color reserved for 'verified' marks — and renders it in a crisp, modern SaaS register rather than a literal paper/ledger pastiche. Nothing about the page tries to look old or textured; the ledger reference is structural (rows, hairlines, tabular alignment), not material.

The system deliberately refuses two category defaults: the dark-navy-plus-neon-gradient 'AI product' look (the incumbent site's previous identity), and the generic three-stat hero-metric wall. Proof lives in one committed comparison chart and a single-row data strip instead, and the marketing page practices what the product preaches — its own headline stat carries a 'see methodology' citation, the same mechanism the product sells.
keyCharacteristics: One committed engineered blue carries brand, primary actions, links, and the chart's 'us' bar — never diluted into a rainbow of accent colors.
A single reserved green exists only for verified/citation marks — a functional color code, never decorative.
Tabular monospace numerals for every stat, price, and quoted citation; proportional Manrope for everything else.
Comparison and association (pricing, market segments) render as rows and tables, never as grids of identical icon-cards.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Exactly one saturated color carries brand and action. A second accent is never introduced for 'variety' — differentiation comes from weight, size, and position.

rules.name: The Green-Means-Verified Rule
rules.body: Green never appears for anything except a citation or verification mark.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Measured Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for numbers, prices, and direct quotes — data with a verifiable source. Never a costume for 'technical'.

rules.name: The Row-Survives Rule
rules.body: Any layout organizing comparable items must keep the row/column relationship legible at every breakpoint — collapse to horizontal scroll before collapsing to a flat unlabeled stack.

rules.name: The One Shadow Rule
rules.body: Only the page's single most important card (the comparison chart) lifts off the ground. Every other card sits flush, bordered, flat.

dos: Do reserve engineered blue for brand, action, and the 'us' data series.
Do render every number, price, and quoted source in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals.
Do keep comparison content in row/table form, collapsing to horizontal scroll rather than a flat stack on narrow screens.
Do use verified-tint background washes for citation/quote emphasis instead of colored borders.
Do label any illustrative/demo content explicitly.
donts: Don't add a kicker or eyebrow badge above a heading.
Don't use a colored border-left/border-right heavier than 1px on any card, list item, or callout.
Don't render comparable sets as identical icon-plus-heading-plus-text cards.
Don't animate width/height/padding/margin for any data visualization or transition.
Don't introduce a second saturated accent color.
Don't use the verified green (#16A34A) as text color.
